speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To begin my evaluation, how long have these symptoms been present, and do they radiate specifically down your arms?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy (or Cervical Radiculopathy) given the chronic progressive course, bilateral upper extremity involvement, and patient's age; however, without imaging, I cannot confirm the level or severity. Given the history of diabetes and hypertension, I need to rule out vascular causes and confirm structural compression. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI. REQUEST TEST: CBC, BMP, HbA1c, TSH, B12.
